name: jomblebee-csharp-solution-explorer
description: A C# Solution Explorer for VS Code and Open VSX editors, with an optional bundled Roslyn language server for IntelliSense — no proprietary extensions required.

csharpSolutionExplorer.confirmMove.description: Ask for confirmation before moving items in the Solution Explorer.

csharpSolutionExplorer.nuget.checkForUpd.description: Check nuget.org for newer versions of direct packages and flag outdated ones in the Dependencies tree.

csharpSolutionExplorer.fileNesting.enabl.description: Group related files under a parent in the Solution Explorer (e.g. appsettings.*.json under appsettings.json, .xaml.cs under .xaml).

csharpSolutionExplorer.autoReveal.description: Automatically select the file of the active editor in the Solution Explorer tree.

csharpSolutionExplorer.templates.class.description: Template for new C# class files. Variables: ${namespace}, ${name}, ${filename}, ${date}, ${cursor} (sets initial cursor position). Clear to show an error instead of creating the file.

csharpSolutionExplorer.templates.interfa.description: Template for new C# interface files. Variables: ${namespace}, ${name}, ${filename}, ${date}, ${cursor} (sets initial cursor position). Clear to show an error instead of creating the file.

csharpSolutionExplorer.templates.record.description: Template for new C# record files. Variables: ${namespace}, ${name}, ${filename}, ${date}, ${cursor} (sets initial cursor position). Clear to show an error instead of creating the file.

csharpSolutionExplorer.templates.enum.description: Template for new C# enum files. Variables: ${namespace}, ${name}, ${filename}, ${date}, ${cursor} (sets initial cursor position). Clear to show an error instead of creating the file.

csharpSolutionExplorer.templates.struct.description: Template for new C# struct files. Variables: ${namespace}, ${name}, ${filename}, ${date}, ${cursor} (sets initial cursor position). Clear to show an error instead of creating the file.

csharpSolutionExplorer.templates.razor.description: Template for new Razor component files (.razor). Variables: ${namespace}, ${name}, ${filename}, ${date}, ${cursor} (sets initial cursor position). Clear to show an error instead of creating the file.

csharpSolutionExplorer.languageServer.en.description: Run the bundled C# language server (Roslyn) for IntelliSense, diagnostics, and hover. The server is downloaded on first use and cached globally. Automatically stays off when the Microsoft C# extension (ms-dotnettools.csharp) is installed, to avoid running two language servers.

csharpSolutionExplorer.languageServer.ve.description: Pin a specific roslyn-language-server version to download from the Roslyn language server feed. Leave empty to use the version bundled with this extension.

csharpSolutionExplorer.languageServer.se.description: Absolute path to a locally installed C# language server (the Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.LanguageServer executable or DLL). When set, the server is used as-is and nothing is downloaded — useful for offline or enterprise environments. Razor cohosting expects the Razor files (RazorExtension.dll, Targets/) next to it, as in the roslyn-language-server package.

csharpSolutionExplorer.languageServer.lo.description: Log verbosity passed to the C# language server (--logLevel).

enumDescriptions: Load a solution if one is found, otherwise all projects in the workspace (default).
Only ever load a solution; never fall back to loose projects.
Always load every .csproj in the workspace and ignore any solution file.
Load only the projects that own the currently-open editors. Referenced projects still load automatically. Evaluated when the server starts.
csharpSolutionExplorer.languageServer.lo.description: What the C# language server loads. Referenced projects (ProjectReference) always load automatically regardless of this setting — it only chooses the entry point.

csharpSolutionExplorer.languageServer.so.description: Path to the specific solution (.sln / .slnx) to load, absolute or relative to the workspace root. Useful when several solutions exist. Leave empty to auto-pick the shallowest one. A non-existent path is ignored. Has no effect in the 'projects' or 'openProjects' load modes.

enumDescriptions: Report errors and warnings only for files you have open (default). Closed files are still understood for navigation and IntelliSense.
Report errors and warnings for every file in the loaded solution/projects, including files you have not opened. Uses more CPU and memory on large solutions.
Do not compute background diagnostics; errors appear only while typing in a file.
csharpSolutionExplorer.languageServer.di.description: How widely the C# language server reports diagnostics (errors/warnings). 'fullSolution' analyzes closed files too. This only affects proactive diagnostics — go-to-definition, find-references, and rename already work across closed files whenever their project is loaded.

csharpSolutionExplorer.languageServer.ra.description: Provide Razor (.razor / .cshtml) language features by cohosting — the Razor service (bundled inside the C# language server package) is loaded into the same process, with no second server. Roslyn handles the C# parts and VS Code's built-in HTML service the HTML parts. The bundled 5.10 server has built-in Razor support, so this works out of the box; an older server set via a version/serverPath override falls back to syntax highlighting only. Has no effect when the C# language server itself is off.

csharpSolutionExplorer.debug.enabled.description: Provide C# debugging using netcoredbg (open source, MIT). The debug adapter is downloaded on the first debug session. Turn this off to remove the debugger entirely, for example when you use another C# debug extension.

enumDescriptions: Always offer C# debug configurations when you press F5.
Offer them unless the Microsoft C# extension is installed, which then owns the zero-configuration path.
Never offer them; a launch.json entry of type 'csharp-netcoredbg' still works.
csharpSolutionExplorer.debug.offerConfig.description: Whether debug configurations from this extension appear in the F5 picker and the Run and Debug dropdown. This covers the picker only: 'csharpSolutionExplorer.debug.handleF5' decides whether F5 skips the picker altogether, and 'Set as Default Debugger' pins this debugger in a launch.json.

csharpSolutionExplorer.debug.handleF5.description: Start the Solution Explorer's startup project when you press F5, with no launch.json and no debugger picker (Ctrl+F5 runs it in an external terminal, without debugging). Applies only while the Microsoft C# extension is not installed and 'offerConfigurations' is not 'never' — otherwise F5 keeps its normal VS Code behaviour. See 'csharpSolutionExplorer.debug.ignoreLaunchJson' for what happens when the workspace also defines its own launch.json. Changes to 'csharpSolutionExplorer.debug.enabled' need a window reload before they apply here.

csharpSolutionExplorer.debug.ignoreLaunc.description: Keep F5 on the Solution Explorer's startup project even when the workspace defines its own launch.json. Turn this off to make a launch.json the escape hatch again — F5 then reverts to VS Code's normal launch.json-driven behaviour whenever the workspace has configurations of its own.

enumDescriptions: F5 launches and owns the program directly; its output goes to the Debug Console. The Debug Console has no usable stdin, so interactive input (Console.ReadKey / Console.ReadLine) does not work.

F5 spawns the program in a VS Code integrated terminal first, then attaches the debugger to it. Gives the program a real, interactive console inside the editor. If the runtime isn't ready for the attach yet, the debugger retries automatically and, if it keeps failing, offers a Retry/Abort notification.

F5 spawns the program in a real external OS terminal first, then attaches the debugger to it — same mechanism as 'Debug Startup Project in External Terminal'. If the runtime isn't ready for the attach yet, the debugger retries automatically and, if it keeps failing, offers a Retry/Abort notification.
csharpSolutionExplorer.debug.f5Console.description: Where F5's program output appears. netcoredbg cannot show real console output (or accept input) for a program it launches directly, so 'integratedTerminal' and 'externalTerminal' work around that by spawning the program in a real terminal first and attaching instead — the only way interactive input works.

csharpSolutionExplorer.debug.buildBefore.description: Build the project before starting a debug session, so breakpoints match the running code.

csharpSolutionExplorer.debug.version.description: netcoredbg release tag to download (e.g. '3.2.0-1092'). Leave empty to use the version bundled with this extension.

csharpSolutionExplorer.debug.debuggerPat.description: Path to a locally built netcoredbg executable (or the folder containing it), used instead of downloading one. Required on platforms with no published build: Intel macOS, Windows on ARM, and musl-based Linux such as Alpine.

csharpSolutionExplorer.debug.logging.description: Write a netcoredbg trace log next to the debug adapter. Only useful when diagnosing debugger problems.

csharpSolutionExplorer.debug.externalTer.description: Milliseconds to delay the program's start after 'Debug Startup Project in External Terminal' opens the terminal, before netcoredbg attaches. netcoredbg cannot launch a program directly into a real console (see that command's tooltip), so this only biases — it does not guarantee — catching breakpoints hit very early in Main(). 0 disables the delay.

csharpSolutionExplorer.testExplorer.enab.description: Show C# test projects in the native Test Explorer, run and debug individual tests, and collect code coverage. Changes need a window reload.

enumDescriptions: A header, build errors and warnings, failing tests, and a final count. Passing tests are not listed.
Everything 'summary' shows plus one line per test result. Restore and build chatter is still dropped.
The test host's log verbatim, including restore and build output.
csharpSolutionExplorer.testExplorer.outp.description: How much of the test host's log goes into the Test Results panel. Build errors and host crashes are always shown, whatever the level, and the full raw log is always available in the 'C# Tests' output channel. Debug runs are always 'full', because the debugger attaches by reading the host's own output.

project.description: Path to the .csproj to debug. Defaults to the Solution Explorer's startup project.

launchProfile.description: Name of the launchSettings.json profile to apply. Defaults to the profile selected in the Solution Explorer.

targetFramework.description: Which framework to debug. Only needed for multi-targeted projects.

configuration.description: Build configuration to build and launch.

program.description: Explicit assembly (.dll) to launch, bypassing project resolution.

args.description: Command line arguments passed to the program.

cwd.description: Working directory of the debugged program.

env.description: Environment variables added to the debugged program.

stopAtEntry.description: Break as soon as the program starts.

console.description: Where the debugged program's output appears. Note: netcoredbg currently always reports program output to the Debug Console regardless of this setting; the Debug Console is revealed automatically when a debug session starts.

processId.description: Process ID of an already-running .NET process to attach to. Prefer the 'Debug Startup Project in External Terminal' command, which spawns the process and fills this in automatically.

program.description: Path to the process's .dll, used for symbol (PDB) resolution.
